detail:
NICHD describes endometriosis as a condition in which tissue similar to the endometrium, the lining of the uterus, grows outside the uterus, most often in the pelvis. The institute notes health care providers do not know the exact cause. Its most common symptoms are pain and infertility, and NICHD estimates it affects a substantial share of women of reproductive age.

Symptoms can include pelvic pain linked to the menstrual cycle, chronic pelvic pain, pain during sex, pain with urination or bowel movements, lower back or thigh pain, heavy periods, and difficulty getting pregnant, though some people have few symptoms. NICHD notes surgery has been the only way to diagnose endometriosis definitively, while providers can sometimes make a probable diagnosis with ultrasound when an ovarian endometriosis cyst is present, alongside history and examination. Untreated disease is described as potentially causing scarring and damage to pelvic organs.

Tabs is not endorsing or verifying this material. Talk to your doctor about endometriosis symptoms and diagnosis.

title: Endometriosis: tissue like the uterine lining growing elsewhere
